title: Count, label and retype the gaps
prompt: Load the messy export (done for you). Set `missing_by_col` to a Series counting missing values per column. In `messy` itself, replace missing channels with `"unknown"` and convert `quantity` to the nullable `"Int64"` dtype, keeping its gaps as missing. Then set `avg_quantity` to the mean of the known quantities, rounded to 2 decimals. Keep all 168 rows: no dropping, and no filling quantities.
hints: Assign the results back: `messy["channel"] = messy["channel"].fillna("unknown")` and `messy["quantity"] = messy["quantity"].astype("Int64")`.
`mean()` skips missing values on its own: `round(float(messy["quantity"].mean()), 2)`.
explanation: The channel gaps get an explicit label because "unknown channel" is useful information in a report, while the quantity gaps stay missing because, until you recover them with the join from Lesson 4.2, no defensible value exists. `Int64` (capital I) keeps the column as whole numbers with `<NA>` for the 9 gaps, instead of the `1.0`, `2.0` floats you started with. `mean()` skips missing values by default, so the average of 1.43 describes the 159 known quantities; filling with 0 first would have produced 1.36, a number that describes no real order.

checks.missing-counts: `missing_by_col` finds 9 missing quantities and 7 missing channels
checks.quantity-int64: `quantity` is `Int64` and still has its 9 gaps
